summary: An indologist and linguist, Constantin D. Georgian studied at the University of Bucharest, the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Leipzig (Ph.D.), learning under Bergaigne, Bréal, Curtius, Leskien, Hübschmann, and Brockhaus. He taught Romanian at Academie für moderne Philologie and Sanskrit at Bucharest.

id: P:Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
summary: A scholar in history, archaeology, philosophy, and linguistics, Constantin François de Chassebœuf studied under Alexander Hamilton. He served as Professor of History at the École Normale Supérieure.

Constantin Régamey worked in Indology, linguistics, and Tibetology, studying at Warsaw (M.A., Ph.D.) and Paris under Schayer, Turczyński, Przyluski, and Lalou. He held posts at Warsaw, served as professor at Lausanne and Fribourg, and presided over the Swiss Asia Society.

Working in linguistics and Indology, Constantine Borissoff completed an MA at Birkbeck, University of London, a Diplom in Oriental Philology at Far Eastern Federal University, and a Higher-Intermediate Certificate in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London.
Cora Du Bois studied at Barnard College and UC Berkeley. She held positions at Hunter College, the Office of Strategic Services, the U.S. Department of State, and Harvard University.

Cora Vreede-de Stuers completed her studies and Ph.D. at the University of Paris, where she also worked as a librarian. She later served as librarian for the Batavian Society, head librarian at Universitas Indonesia, and lecturer at the University of Amsterdam.

A scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, Corinna May Lhoir pursued doctoral studies at Ghent University and the University of Hamburg. At Hamburg, she is attested in 2026 as a lecturer and yoga studies program coordinator.

Corneille Jest was a Tibetology and archaeology scholar who studied at Paris Descartes University and under André Leroi-Gourhan. From around 1956 to 1995, he held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Specializing in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Cornelis Jan Kuiken earned his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under the supervision of Timothy Hugh Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer, having earlier studied under MA supervisor Jaap den Hollander.

A scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Cornelis Petrus Tiele studied at the Athenaeum Illustre, Remonstrant Seminary, and University of Amsterdam. He served as professor at the Remonstrant Seminary and Leiden University, and Gifford Lecturer at Edinburgh.

id: P:Cornelius Wilhelmus Josef van der Linden
summary: Cornelius Wilhelmus Josef van der Linden was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Utrecht University in 1954 under the doctoral supervision of Jan Gonda.
Corrado Pensa, working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. He served as a professor at Sapienza University of Rome, attested in 1971.
Cortland Dahl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche, Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

Courtney Bruntz specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a professorship at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and serves as Professor of East Asian Buddhism and assessment director at the Numata Center (attested 2026).

A specialist in Indology and Buddhist studies, Craig Jamieson served at the University of Cambridge, including as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection, and became a fellow of Queens' College.
Craig Preston, who specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Virginia and under Joe Bransford Wilson and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Cristina Pecchia works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Sapienza University of Rome and studied at Vienna, learning under Gnoli, Torella, Pensa, and Steinkellner, later holding research and lecturing roles at Vienna and IKGA.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Cristina Scherrer-Schaub served as a professor at the University of Lausanne from circa 1998 to 2012 and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 2000 to 2016.

An Indologist, Csaba Dezső earned master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. Around 2004, he served as an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.

Indologist Csaba Kiss completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" from 2019 to 2024 and is attested as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.
